original_question: Are strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds of real dimension 5 locally embeddable?
target_in_paper: The draft matches the remark following Theorem 1 in §2 ("Codimension one"): for abstract strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds, real dimension 5 is singled out as an open local embeddability case, and the paper immediately adds that this is equivalent to the open Poincaré-lemma problem for (0,1)-forms in the same dimension. The arXiv identifier in the prompt appears mismatched, since arXiv:math/9509202 is "The Several Complex Variables Problem List," while the matching paper is Brinkschulte–Hill–Nacinovich, "The Poincaré lemma and local embeddability." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core issue highlighted by the paper: the real-dimension-5, strictly/strongly pseudoconvex CR case and the question of local CR embeddability. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
missing_details: The paper is about smooth abstract CR manifolds, not necessarily CR manifolds already realized as embedded submanifolds of some complex manifold. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
The relevant setting is hypersurface type, namely CR type (2,1): real dimension 5 means CR dimension 2 and CR codimension 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
The question is pointwise and local: one fixes a point p in M and assumes strict pseudoconvexity at p, i.e. positivity of the Levi form there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
The paper's notion of local embeddability is local CR embeddability into complex Euclidean space; in this case it means a local CR embedding into C^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))

More explicitly, local embeddability is formulated via smooth complex-valued CR functions with linearly independent differentials, not merely via a smooth manifold embedding. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
The paper presents this as an open problem in dimension 5, not as a theorem with a yes/no answer. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))

The nearest explicit equivalent reformulation in the paper is the validity of the Poincaré lemma for the tangential Cauchy–Riemann operator \bar\partial_M on smooth (0,1)-forms at p. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
The paper's terminology is 'strictly pseudoconvex' rather than 'strongly pseudoconvex,' so that is the sharper paper-faithful phrasing. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
refined_question: Let M be a smooth abstract CR manifold of type (2,1) (equivalently, a CR hypersurface of real dimension 5), and let p ∈ M. If M is strictly pseudoconvex at p, must M be locally CR embeddable at p into C^3; equivalently, is there a neighborhood U of p and three smooth complex-valued CR functions on U whose differentials are linearly independent? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation proved in the paper: let M be a smooth abstract CR manifold of type (2,1), and let p ∈ M be a strictly pseudoconvex point. Does the Poincaré lemma for the tangential Cauchy–Riemann operator \bar\partial_M on smooth (0,1)-forms hold at p; that is, for every neighborhood Ω of p and every smooth (0,1)-form f on Ω with \bar\partial_M f = 0, does there exist a smaller neighborhood ω of p and a smooth function u on ω such that \bar\partial_M u = f on ω? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
justification: Section 1 provides exactly the hidden definitions needed to make the question stand alone: abstract CR manifold of type (n,k), local embeddability, and the Poincaré lemma for (0,1)-forms. Section 2 specializes to codimension one and proves Theorem 1: at a strictly pseudoconvex point, local embeddability is equivalent to the Poincaré lemma for smooth (0,1)-forms. The subsequent remark then identifies dimension 5 as the open case for abstract strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds. Because your draft asks precisely about local embeddability in real dimension 5, the narrowest faithful rewrite is the type-(2,1), pointwise, local CR-embedding question above, with the Poincaré-lemma version as the only paper-explicit alternate formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))
